Your AI is only as good as the data infrastructure underneath it.

A major new study just quantified what many executives have sensed but few have measured: 1 in 5 enterprise workers lose a full workday every week manually moving data between systems that cannot talk to each other.

The Harris Poll surveyed 6,100 enterprise decision-makers globally and the finding is stark — the primary bottleneck in enterprise AI is not model capability. It is integration. Workers are copying, reformatting, and reconciling data across disconnected platforms instead of doing the work AI was supposed to accelerate.

This means organizations that invested heavily in AI without first re-engineering their data pipelines are paying a hidden productivity tax every single week. And it compounds.

The executives seeing real returns from AI share one pattern: they treated data architecture and system integration as a strategic priority before deploying intelligent agents. Not after.

If your team is spending hours on data handoffs that no one has quantified, that is where your AI ROI is leaking.
